results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019-2020 Altima and 2018-2021 Titan vehicles equipped with Continental tires.  On the affected vehicles, it is possible that one or more tires were cured for too long during tire production.
results.Consequence: Over cured tires may develop a break in the sidewall, resulting in sudden air loss or belt edge separation which could lead to tread/belt loss.  Either condition can cause a loss of vehicle control, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners, and dealers will inspect the tires, and replace them as necessary, free of charge.  Owner notification letters were mailed on May 11, 2021.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.  Nissan's number for this recall is PC798.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019 Altima vehicles equipped with front wheel drive (FWD) and 2.5 liter engines.  The fuel pump lock ring may not be fully engaged, possibly causing fuel to leak.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 301, "Fuel System Integrity."
results.Consequence: A fuel leak in the presence of an ignition source increases the risk of a fire.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners, and dealers will inspect the fuel tank assembly. If the lock ring is disengaged, dealers will tighten the ring to specification. If the lock ring is detached, dealers will replace the fuel pump.  Both remedies will be completed free of charge. The recall began May 15, 2019. Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019 Altima vehicles.  The retainer clip connecting the low pressure fuel tube to the high pressure fuel pump may not have been locked into position.
results.Consequence: If the retainer clip is unlocked, the fuel tube may shift and cause a fuel leak, increasing the risk of a fire.  If the fuel tube fully disconnects, the engine can stall, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan has notified owners, and dealers will route the fuel hose into the holding clip and lock the retainer clip into place, as necessary, free of charge.  The recall began February 11, 2019.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019 Nissan Altima vehicles.  The brake switch bracket may be in the incorrect location, which may cause the brake switch to remain on.
results.Consequence: If the brake switch remains in the ON position, the brake lights will remain illuminated when the brakes are not being pressed, which may confuse other drivers.  Additionally, the transmission shift lever may be moved out of the Park position without the brake pedal being pressed, allowing the vehicle to roll unexpectedly.  Either condition increases the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners, and dealers will inspect and install a new brake pedal as needed, free of charge.  The recall began May 15, 2019.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Component: BACK OVER PREVENTION: SENSING SYSTEM: CAMERA
results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2018-2019 Nissan Altima, Armada, Frontier, Kicks, Leaf, Maxima, Murano, NV, NV200, Pathfinder, Rogue, Rogue Sport, Sentra, Titan, Titan Diesel, Versa Note and Versa Sedan vehicles, as well as Infiniti Q50, Q60, QX30 and QX80 vehicles.  Additionally included are 2019 Nissan GT-R and Taxi and Infiniti QX50, QX60, Q70, Q70L vehicles.  The back-up camera and display settings can be adjusted such that the rear view image is no longer visible and the system will retain that setting the next time the vehicle is placed in reverse.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 111, "Rear Visibility."
results.Consequence: The lack of an image in the back-up camera display increases the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners in phases, having dealers update the back-up camera settings software, free of charge.  The recall began November 11, 2019 and all affected VINs should be activated.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669 or INFINITI customer service at 1-800-662-6200.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Component: BACK OVER PREVENTION: SENSING SYSTEM: CAMERA
results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019-2021 Altima and 2020-2021 Sentra vehicles.  Damage to the camera harness can cause distortion or loss of the rearview camera display image.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard number 111, "Rear Visibility."
results.Consequence: A rearview camera that does not properly display an image can reduce the driver's rear view, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Dealers will inspect the rearview camera and harness for damage and replace them as necessary.  If no damage is found, the dealer will apply protective tape and reroute the rearview camera harness.  Repairs will be performed free of charge.  Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed October 19, 2023.  Owners may contact Nissan's customer service at 1-800-867-7669.  Nissan's number for this recall is R23C3.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.nhtsa.gov.

results.Component: ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING:ENGINE:HARD PARTS INTERNAL/MECHANICAL
results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2021-2024 Rogue, 2019-2020 Altima, 2019-2022 Infiniti QX50, and 2022 Infiniti QX55 vehicles equipped with 3-cylinder 1.5L or 4-cylinder 2.0L variable compression turbo (VC-Turbo) engines. The engine bearings may have manufacturing defects that can lead to engine failure.
results.Consequence: Engine failure increases the risk of a crash. A bearing failure may cause a breach in the engine block, allowing hot oil to be discharged, increasing the risk of an engine fire.
results.Remedy: Dealers will reprogram the engine control module (ECM) software, free of charge. Owner letters were mailed April 8, 2026. Owners may contact Nissan's customer service at 800-647-7261 or Infiniti's customer service at 1-800-662-6200. Nissan's numbers for this recall are R25A8/A9 and R25B1/B2.

Owners may contact Nissan's customer service at 800-647-7261 or Infiniti's customer service at 1-800-662-6200. Nissan's numbers for this recall are R25A8/A9 and R25B1/B2.

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019-2020 Altima and 2018-2021 Titan vehicles equipped with Continental tires.  On the affected vehicles, it is possible that one or more tires were cured for too long during tire production.
results.Consequence: Over cured tires may develop a break in the sidewall, resulting in sudden air loss or belt edge separation which could lead to tread/belt loss.  Either condition can cause a loss of vehicle control, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners, and dealers will inspect the tires, and replace them as necessary, free of charge.  Owner notification letters were mailed on May 11, 2021.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.  Nissan's number for this recall is PC798.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019 Altima vehicles equipped with front wheel drive (FWD) and 2.5 liter engines.  The fuel pump lock ring may not be fully engaged, possibly causing fuel to leak.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 301, "Fuel System Integrity."
results.Consequence: A fuel leak in the presence of an ignition source increases the risk of a fire.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners, and dealers will inspect the fuel tank assembly. If the lock ring is disengaged, dealers will tighten the ring to specification. If the lock ring is detached, dealers will replace the fuel pump.  Both remedies will be completed free of charge. The recall began May 15, 2019. Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019 Altima vehicles.  The retainer clip connecting the low pressure fuel tube to the high pressure fuel pump may not have been locked into position.
results.Consequence: If the retainer clip is unlocked, the fuel tube may shift and cause a fuel leak, increasing the risk of a fire.  If the fuel tube fully disconnects, the engine can stall, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan has notified owners, and dealers will route the fuel hose into the holding clip and lock the retainer clip into place, as necessary, free of charge.  The recall began February 11, 2019.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019 Nissan Altima vehicles.  The brake switch bracket may be in the incorrect location, which may cause the brake switch to remain on.
results.Consequence: If the brake switch remains in the ON position, the brake lights will remain illuminated when the brakes are not being pressed, which may confuse other drivers.  Additionally, the transmission shift lever may be moved out of the Park position without the brake pedal being pressed, allowing the vehicle to roll unexpectedly.  Either condition increases the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners, and dealers will inspect and install a new brake pedal as needed, free of charge.  The recall began May 15, 2019.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2018-2019 Nissan Altima, Armada, Frontier, Kicks, Leaf, Maxima, Murano, NV, NV200, Pathfinder, Rogue, Rogue Sport, Sentra, Titan, Titan Diesel, Versa Note and Versa Sedan vehicles, as well as Infiniti Q50, Q60, QX30 and QX80 vehicles.  Additionally included are 2019 Nissan GT-R and Taxi and Infiniti QX50, QX60, Q70, Q70L vehicles.  The back-up camera and display settings can be adjusted such that the rear view image is no longer visible and the system will retain that setting the next time the vehicle is placed in reverse.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 111, "Rear Visibility."
results.Consequence: The lack of an image in the back-up camera display increases the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners in phases, having dealers update the back-up camera settings software, free of charge.  The recall began November 11, 2019 and all affected VINs should be activated.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669 or INFINITI customer service at 1-800-662-6200.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Component: BACK OVER PREVENTION: SENSING SYSTEM: CAMERA
results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019-2021 Altima and 2020-2021 Sentra vehicles.  Damage to the camera harness can cause distortion or loss of the rearview camera display image.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard number 111, "Rear Visibility."
results.Consequence: A rearview camera that does not properly display an image can reduce the driver's rear view, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Dealers will inspect the rearview camera and harness for damage and replace them as necessary.  If no damage is found, the dealer will apply protective tape and reroute the rearview camera harness.  Repairs will be performed free of charge.  Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed October 19, 2023.  Owners may contact Nissan's customer service at 1-800-867-7669.  Nissan's number for this recall is R23C3.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.nhtsa.gov.

results.Component: ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING:ENGINE:HARD PARTS INTERNAL/MECHANICAL
results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2021-2024 Rogue, 2019-2020 Altima, 2019-2022 Infiniti QX50, and 2022 Infiniti QX55 vehicles equipped with 3-cylinder 1.5L or 4-cylinder 2.0L variable compression turbo (VC-Turbo) engines. The engine bearings may have manufacturing defects that can lead to engine failure.
results.Consequence: Engine failure increases the risk of a crash. A bearing failure may cause a breach in the engine block, allowing hot oil to be discharged, increasing the risk of an engine fire.
results.Remedy: Dealers will reprogram the engine control module (ECM) software, free of charge. Owner letters were mailed April 8, 2026. Owners may contact Nissan's customer service at 800-647-7261 or Infiniti's customer service at 1-800-662-6200. Nissan's numbers for this recall are R25A8/A9 and R25B1/B2.

The police report authored by Officer #8927 documents the tread separation at the scene, providing an independent contemporaneous record linking the defect to the loss event. Because the recalled defect is the proximate cause of the blowout, product liability exposure attaches to the tire/vehicle manufacturer, making them the appropriate subrogation target. California's pure comparative negligence doctrine reduces the recoverable share to 40% of the $5,200 gross exposure — yielding the rules-engine demand of $2,080 — because the insured has been assessed at 60% fault. risks: Causation challenge: The opposing party will argue that the tread separation was caused by road hazard, improper inflation, overloading, or driver neglect rather than the recalled manufacturing defect — especially since evidence strength is only MODERATE and physical tire evidence has not yet been secured.

Recall remedy defense: If the manufacturer can show that the recall remedy (e.g., tire replacement) was made available and the insured failed to respond to the recall notice, they may argue the insured's inaction was a superseding cause, potentially increasing the insured's comparative fault beyond 60%.

Insured's high fault share: At 60% comparative fault, the insured's own conduct (speed, road conditions, vehicle maintenance) will be scrutinized; the defense may seek to push that percentage higher, further eroding the recoverable demand below the $2,080 figure.

Chain-of-custody / evidence preservation: Without the physical tire in custody, the defense will challenge whether the tread separation pattern is consistent with the specific defect described in campaign 21V169000, potentially defeating the recall-to-loss-cause linkage.

Statute of limitations / tolling disputes: Although 406 days remain, delays in obtaining the physical tire, recall remedy records, and expert analysis could compress the timeline; the defense may also contest the accrual date of the claim.

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019-2020 Altima and 2018-2021 Titan vehicles equipped with Continental tires.  On the affected vehicles, it is possible that one or more tires were cured for too long during tire production.
results.Consequence: Over cured tires may develop a break in the sidewall, resulting in sudden air loss or belt edge separation which could lead to tread/belt loss.  Either condition can cause a loss of vehicle control, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners, and dealers will inspect the tires, and replace them as necessary, free of charge.  Owner notification letters were mailed on May 11, 2021.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.  Nissan's number for this recall is PC798.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019 Altima vehicles equipped with front wheel drive (FWD) and 2.5 liter engines.  The fuel pump lock ring may not be fully engaged, possibly causing fuel to leak.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 301, "Fuel System Integrity."
results.Consequence: A fuel leak in the presence of an ignition source increases the risk of a fire.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners, and dealers will inspect the fuel tank assembly. If the lock ring is disengaged, dealers will tighten the ring to specification. If the lock ring is detached, dealers will replace the fuel pump.  Both remedies will be completed free of charge. The recall began May 15, 2019. Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019 Altima vehicles.  The retainer clip connecting the low pressure fuel tube to the high pressure fuel pump may not have been locked into position.
results.Consequence: If the retainer clip is unlocked, the fuel tube may shift and cause a fuel leak, increasing the risk of a fire.  If the fuel tube fully disconnects, the engine can stall, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan has notified owners, and dealers will route the fuel hose into the holding clip and lock the retainer clip into place, as necessary, free of charge.  The recall began February 11, 2019.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019 Nissan Altima vehicles.  The brake switch bracket may be in the incorrect location, which may cause the brake switch to remain on.
results.Consequence: If the brake switch remains in the ON position, the brake lights will remain illuminated when the brakes are not being pressed, which may confuse other drivers.  Additionally, the transmission shift lever may be moved out of the Park position without the brake pedal being pressed, allowing the vehicle to roll unexpectedly.  Either condition increases the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners, and dealers will inspect and install a new brake pedal as needed, free of charge.  The recall began May 15, 2019.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Component: BACK OVER PREVENTION: SENSING SYSTEM: CAMERA
results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2018-2019 Nissan Altima, Armada, Frontier, Kicks, Leaf, Maxima, Murano, NV, NV200, Pathfinder, Rogue, Rogue Sport, Sentra, Titan, Titan Diesel, Versa Note and Versa Sedan vehicles, as well as Infiniti Q50, Q60, QX30 and QX80 vehicles.  Additionally included are 2019 Nissan GT-R and Taxi and Infiniti QX50, QX60, Q70, Q70L vehicles.  The back-up camera and display settings can be adjusted such that the rear view image is no longer visible and the system will retain that setting the next time the vehicle is placed in reverse.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 111, "Rear Visibility."
results.Consequence: The lack of an image in the back-up camera display increases the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners in phases, having dealers update the back-up camera settings software, free of charge.  The recall began November 11, 2019 and all affected VINs should be activated.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669 or INFINITI customer service at 1-800-662-6200.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Component: BACK OVER PREVENTION: SENSING SYSTEM: CAMERA
results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019-2021 Altima and 2020-2021 Sentra vehicles.  Damage to the camera harness can cause distortion or loss of the rearview camera display image.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard number 111, "Rear Visibility."
results.Consequence: A rearview camera that does not properly display an image can reduce the driver's rear view, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Dealers will inspect the rearview camera and harness for damage and replace them as necessary.  If no damage is found, the dealer will apply protective tape and reroute the rearview camera harness.  Repairs will be performed free of charge.  Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed October 19, 2023.  Owners may contact Nissan's customer service at 1-800-867-7669.  Nissan's number for this recall is R23C3.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.nhtsa.gov.

results.Component: ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING:ENGINE:HARD PARTS INTERNAL/MECHANICAL
results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2021-2024 Rogue, 2019-2020 Altima, 2019-2022 Infiniti QX50, and 2022 Infiniti QX55 vehicles equipped with 3-cylinder 1.5L or 4-cylinder 2.0L variable compression turbo (VC-Turbo) engines. The engine bearings may have manufacturing defects that can lead to engine failure.
results.Consequence: Engine failure increases the risk of a crash. A bearing failure may cause a breach in the engine block, allowing hot oil to be discharged, increasing the risk of an engine fire.
results.Remedy: Dealers will reprogram the engine control module (ECM) software, free of charge. Owner letters were mailed April 8, 2026. Owners may contact Nissan's customer service at 800-647-7261 or Infiniti's customer service at 1-800-662-6200. Nissan's numbers for this recall are R25A8/A9 and R25B1/B2.

NHTSA recall campaign 21V169000 covers a TIRES component defect on vehicles matching this make, model, and model year, directly linking the recalled tire defect to the mechanism of loss. The tread separation failure mode described at the scene is consistent with the type of tire structural defect addressed by campaign 21V169000. Under California's pure comparative negligence doctrine, the insured is assessed at 60% fault, leaving a 40% recoverable fault factor attributable to the other party, yielding a calculated demand of $2,080 against a gross subrogation exposure of $5,200. The statute of limitations has approximately 406 days remaining, providing adequate time to pursue recovery. Overall, the recall-to-loss-cause linkage is supported by the police report and the matched NHTSA campaign, but physical tire evidence and recall remedy records are needed to solidify the claim.
gaps: Physical tire evidence: The failed front tire should be preserved, inspected, and photographed by a qualified tire forensic expert to confirm tread separation consistent with the defect described in NHTSA campaign 21V169000.

Recall remedy records: Obtain documentation from Nissan or the dealership network confirming whether the recall remedy was or was not performed on VIN 1N4BL4BV5KB570668 prior to the loss date — an unperformed remedy strengthens the subrogation theory against the manufacturer or dealer.
NHTSA campaign 21V169000 full details: Retrieve the complete campaign document (affected VIN range, defect description, remedy) to confirm this specific VIN falls within the recall population.

Tire manufacturer identification: Identify the tire brand, model, DOT code, and manufacture date from the failed tire to determine whether a separate products liability claim against the tire manufacturer is viable.
Other-party insurance information: Confirm the adverse party's carrier and policy limits to assess collectability against the 40% fault share.
Repair/total-loss documentation: Obtain final repair invoices or total-loss valuation to substantiate the $4,700 paid amount and $5,200 gross subrogation figure.

risks: Causation challenge: The opposing party will argue that the tread separation was caused by road hazard, improper inflation, overloading, or driver neglect rather than the recalled manufacturing defect — especially since evidence strength is only MODERATE and physical tire evidence has not yet been secured.

Recall remedy defense: If the manufacturer can show that the recall remedy (e.g., tire replacement) was made available and the insured failed to respond to the recall notice, they may argue the insured's inaction was a superseding cause, potentially increasing the insured's comparative fault beyond 60%.

Insured's high fault share: At 60% comparative fault, the insured's own conduct (speed, road conditions, vehicle maintenance) will be scrutinized; the defense may seek to push that percentage higher, further eroding the recoverable demand below the $2,080 figure.

Chain-of-custody / evidence preservation: Without the physical tire in custody, the defense will challenge whether the tread separation pattern is consistent with the specific defect described in campaign 21V169000, potentially defeating the recall-to-loss-cause linkage.

Statute of limitations / tolling disputes: Although 406 days remain, delays in obtaining the physical tire, recall remedy records, and expert analysis could compress the timeline; the defense may also contest the accrual date of the claim.

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019-2020 Altima and 2018-2021 Titan vehicles equipped with Continental tires.  On the affected vehicles, it is possible that one or more tires were cured for too long during tire production.
results.Consequence: Over cured tires may develop a break in the sidewall, resulting in sudden air loss or belt edge separation which could lead to tread/belt loss.  Either condition can cause a loss of vehicle control, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners, and dealers will inspect the tires, and replace them as necessary, free of charge.  Owner notification letters were mailed on May 11, 2021.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.  Nissan's number for this recall is PC798.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019 Altima vehicles equipped with front wheel drive (FWD) and 2.5 liter engines.  The fuel pump lock ring may not be fully engaged, possibly causing fuel to leak.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 301, "Fuel System Integrity."
results.Consequence: A fuel leak in the presence of an ignition source increases the risk of a fire.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners, and dealers will inspect the fuel tank assembly. If the lock ring is disengaged, dealers will tighten the ring to specification. If the lock ring is detached, dealers will replace the fuel pump.  Both remedies will be completed free of charge. The recall began May 15, 2019. Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019 Altima vehicles.  The retainer clip connecting the low pressure fuel tube to the high pressure fuel pump may not have been locked into position.
results.Consequence: If the retainer clip is unlocked, the fuel tube may shift and cause a fuel leak, increasing the risk of a fire.  If the fuel tube fully disconnects, the engine can stall, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan has notified owners, and dealers will route the fuel hose into the holding clip and lock the retainer clip into place, as necessary, free of charge.  The recall began February 11, 2019.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019 Nissan Altima vehicles.  The brake switch bracket may be in the incorrect location, which may cause the brake switch to remain on.
results.Consequence: If the brake switch remains in the ON position, the brake lights will remain illuminated when the brakes are not being pressed, which may confuse other drivers.  Additionally, the transmission shift lever may be moved out of the Park position without the brake pedal being pressed, allowing the vehicle to roll unexpectedly.  Either condition increases the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners, and dealers will inspect and install a new brake pedal as needed, free of charge.  The recall began May 15, 2019.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Component: BACK OVER PREVENTION: SENSING SYSTEM: CAMERA
results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2018-2019 Nissan Altima, Armada, Frontier, Kicks, Leaf, Maxima, Murano, NV, NV200, Pathfinder, Rogue, Rogue Sport, Sentra, Titan, Titan Diesel, Versa Note and Versa Sedan vehicles, as well as Infiniti Q50, Q60, QX30 and QX80 vehicles.  Additionally included are 2019 Nissan GT-R and Taxi and Infiniti QX50, QX60, Q70, Q70L vehicles.  The back-up camera and display settings can be adjusted such that the rear view image is no longer visible and the system will retain that setting the next time the vehicle is placed in reverse.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 111, "Rear Visibility."
results.Consequence: The lack of an image in the back-up camera display increases the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners in phases, having dealers update the back-up camera settings software, free of charge.  The recall began November 11, 2019 and all affected VINs should be activated.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669 or INFINITI customer service at 1-800-662-6200.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Component: BACK OVER PREVENTION: SENSING SYSTEM: CAMERA
results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019-2021 Altima and 2020-2021 Sentra vehicles.  Damage to the camera harness can cause distortion or loss of the rearview camera display image.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard number 111, "Rear Visibility."
results.Consequence: A rearview camera that does not properly display an image can reduce the driver's rear view, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Dealers will inspect the rearview camera and harness for damage and replace them as necessary.  If no damage is found, the dealer will apply protective tape and reroute the rearview camera harness.  Repairs will be performed free of charge.  Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed October 19, 2023.  Owners may contact Nissan's customer service at 1-800-867-7669.  Nissan's number for this recall is R23C3.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.nhtsa.gov.

results.Component: ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING:ENGINE:HARD PARTS INTERNAL/MECHANICAL
results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2021-2024 Rogue, 2019-2020 Altima, 2019-2022 Infiniti QX50, and 2022 Infiniti QX55 vehicles equipped with 3-cylinder 1.5L or 4-cylinder 2.0L variable compression turbo (VC-Turbo) engines. The engine bearings may have manufacturing defects that can lead to engine failure.
results.Consequence: Engine failure increases the risk of a crash. A bearing failure may cause a breach in the engine block, allowing hot oil to be discharged, increasing the risk of an engine fire.
results.Remedy: Dealers will reprogram the engine control module (ECM) software, free of charge. Owner letters were mailed April 8, 2026. Owners may contact Nissan's customer service at 800-647-7261 or Infiniti's customer service at 1-800-662-6200. Nissan's numbers for this recall are R25A8/A9 and R25B1/B2.

state.rationale: The 2019 Nissan Altima experienced a front-tire tread separation on 2024-12-15, a failure mode directly addressed by NHTSA recall campaign 21V169000, which covers a known TIRES component defect on this exact make, model, and model year. The police report authored by Officer #8927 documents the tread separation at the scene, providing an independent contemporaneous record linking the defect to the loss event. Because the recalled defect is the proximate cause of the blowout, product liability exposure attaches to the tire/vehicle manufacturer, making them the appropriate subrogation target. California's pure comparative negligence doctrine reduces the recoverable share to 40% of the $5,200 gross exposure — yielding the rules-engine demand of $2,080 — because the insured has been assessed at 60% fault. With 406 days remaining on the statute of limitations, there is adequate time to develop the physical evidence and pursue the demand before the deadline.

The tread separation failure mode described at the scene is consistent with the type of tire structural defect addressed by campaign 21V169000. Under California's pure comparative negligence doctrine, the insured is assessed at 60% fault, leaving a 40% recoverable fault factor attributable to the other party, yielding a calculated demand of $2,080 against a gross subrogation exposure of $5,200. The statute of limitations has approximately 406 days remaining, providing adequate time to pursue recovery. Overall, the recall-to-loss-cause linkage is supported by the police report and the matched NHTSA campaign, but physical tire evidence and recall remedy records are needed to solidify the claim.

liabilityAssessor.output.rationale: The 2019 Nissan Altima experienced a front-tire tread separation on 2024-12-15, a failure mode directly addressed by NHTSA recall campaign 21V169000, which covers a known TIRES component defect on this exact make, model, and model year. The police report authored by Officer #8927 documents the tread separation at the scene, providing an independent contemporaneous record linking the defect to the loss event. Because the recalled defect is the proximate cause of the blowout, product liability exposure attaches to the tire/vehicle manufacturer, making them the appropriate subrogation target. California's pure comparative negligence doctrine reduces the recoverable share to 40% of the $5,200 gross exposure — yielding the rules-engine demand of $2,080 — because the insured has been assessed at 60% fault. With 406 days remaining on the statute of limitations, there is adequate time to develop the physical evidence and pursue the demand before the deadline.
risks: Causation challenge: The opposing party will argue that the tread separation was caused by road hazard, improper inflation, overloading, or driver neglect rather than the recalled manufacturing defect — especially since evidence strength is only MODERATE and physical tire evidence has not yet been secured.

Recall remedy defense: If the manufacturer can show that the recall remedy (e.g., tire replacement) was made available and the insured failed to respond to the recall notice, they may argue the insured's inaction was a superseding cause, potentially increasing the insured's comparative fault beyond 60%.

Insured's high fault share: At 60% comparative fault, the insured's own conduct (speed, road conditions, vehicle maintenance) will be scrutinized; the defense may seek to push that percentage higher, further eroding the recoverable demand below the $2,080 figure.

Chain-of-custody / evidence preservation: Without the physical tire in custody, the defense will challenge whether the tread separation pattern is consistent with the specific defect described in campaign 21V169000, potentially defeating the recall-to-loss-cause linkage.

Statute of limitations / tolling disputes: Although 406 days remain, delays in obtaining the physical tire, recall remedy records, and expert analysis could compress the timeline; the defense may also contest the accrual date of the claim.

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019-2020 Altima and 2018-2021 Titan vehicles equipped with Continental tires.  On the affected vehicles, it is possible that one or more tires were cured for too long during tire production.
results.Consequence: Over cured tires may develop a break in the sidewall, resulting in sudden air loss or belt edge separation which could lead to tread/belt loss.  Either condition can cause a loss of vehicle control, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners, and dealers will inspect the tires, and replace them as necessary, free of charge.  Owner notification letters were mailed on May 11, 2021.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.  Nissan's number for this recall is PC798.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019 Altima vehicles equipped with front wheel drive (FWD) and 2.5 liter engines.  The fuel pump lock ring may not be fully engaged, possibly causing fuel to leak.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 301, "Fuel System Integrity."
results.Consequence: A fuel leak in the presence of an ignition source increases the risk of a fire.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners, and dealers will inspect the fuel tank assembly. If the lock ring is disengaged, dealers will tighten the ring to specification. If the lock ring is detached, dealers will replace the fuel pump.  Both remedies will be completed free of charge. The recall began May 15, 2019. Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019 Altima vehicles.  The retainer clip connecting the low pressure fuel tube to the high pressure fuel pump may not have been locked into position.
results.Consequence: If the retainer clip is unlocked, the fuel tube may shift and cause a fuel leak, increasing the risk of a fire.  If the fuel tube fully disconnects, the engine can stall, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan has notified owners, and dealers will route the fuel hose into the holding clip and lock the retainer clip into place, as necessary, free of charge.  The recall began February 11, 2019.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019 Nissan Altima vehicles.  The brake switch bracket may be in the incorrect location, which may cause the brake switch to remain on.
results.Consequence: If the brake switch remains in the ON position, the brake lights will remain illuminated when the brakes are not being pressed, which may confuse other drivers.  Additionally, the transmission shift lever may be moved out of the Park position without the brake pedal being pressed, allowing the vehicle to roll unexpectedly.  Either condition increases the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners, and dealers will inspect and install a new brake pedal as needed, free of charge.  The recall began May 15, 2019.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Component: BACK OVER PREVENTION: SENSING SYSTEM: CAMERA
results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2018-2019 Nissan Altima, Armada, Frontier, Kicks, Leaf, Maxima, Murano, NV, NV200, Pathfinder, Rogue, Rogue Sport, Sentra, Titan, Titan Diesel, Versa Note and Versa Sedan vehicles, as well as Infiniti Q50, Q60, QX30 and QX80 vehicles.  Additionally included are 2019 Nissan GT-R and Taxi and Infiniti QX50, QX60, Q70, Q70L vehicles.  The back-up camera and display settings can be adjusted such that the rear view image is no longer visible and the system will retain that setting the next time the vehicle is placed in reverse.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 111, "Rear Visibility."
results.Consequence: The lack of an image in the back-up camera display increases the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners in phases, having dealers update the back-up camera settings software, free of charge.  The recall began November 11, 2019 and all affected VINs should be activated.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669 or INFINITI customer service at 1-800-662-6200.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Component: BACK OVER PREVENTION: SENSING SYSTEM: CAMERA
results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019-2021 Altima and 2020-2021 Sentra vehicles.  Damage to the camera harness can cause distortion or loss of the rearview camera display image.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard number 111, "Rear Visibility."
results.Consequence: A rearview camera that does not properly display an image can reduce the driver's rear view, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Dealers will inspect the rearview camera and harness for damage and replace them as necessary.  If no damage is found, the dealer will apply protective tape and reroute the rearview camera harness.  Repairs will be performed free of charge.  Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed October 19, 2023.  Owners may contact Nissan's customer service at 1-800-867-7669.  Nissan's number for this recall is R23C3.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.nhtsa.gov.

results.Component: ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING:ENGINE:HARD PARTS INTERNAL/MECHANICAL
results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2021-2024 Rogue, 2019-2020 Altima, 2019-2022 Infiniti QX50, and 2022 Infiniti QX55 vehicles equipped with 3-cylinder 1.5L or 4-cylinder 2.0L variable compression turbo (VC-Turbo) engines. The engine bearings may have manufacturing defects that can lead to engine failure.
results.Consequence: Engine failure increases the risk of a crash. A bearing failure may cause a breach in the engine block, allowing hot oil to be discharged, increasing the risk of an engine fire.
results.Remedy: Dealers will reprogram the engine control module (ECM) software, free of charge. Owner letters were mailed April 8, 2026. Owners may contact Nissan's customer service at 800-647-7261 or Infiniti's customer service at 1-800-662-6200. Nissan's numbers for this recall are R25A8/A9 and R25B1/B2.

NHTSA recall campaign 21V169000 covers a TIRES component defect on vehicles matching this make, model, and model year, directly linking the recalled tire defect to the mechanism of loss. The tread separation failure mode described at the scene is consistent with the type of tire structural defect addressed by campaign 21V169000. Under California's pure comparative negligence doctrine, the insured is assessed at 60% fault, leaving a 40% recoverable fault factor attributable to the other party, yielding a calculated demand of $2,080 against a gross subrogation exposure of $5,200. The statute of limitations has approximately 406 days remaining, providing adequate time to pursue recovery. Overall, the recall-to-loss-cause linkage is supported by the police report and the matched NHTSA campaign, but physical tire evidence and recall remedy records are needed to solidify the claim.
gaps: Physical tire evidence: The failed front tire should be preserved, inspected, and photographed by a qualified tire forensic expert to confirm tread separation consistent with the defect described in NHTSA campaign 21V169000.

Recall remedy records: Obtain documentation from Nissan or the dealership network confirming whether the recall remedy was or was not performed on VIN 1N4BL4BV5KB570668 prior to the loss date — an unperformed remedy strengthens the subrogation theory against the manufacturer or dealer.
NHTSA campaign 21V169000 full details: Retrieve the complete campaign document (affected VIN range, defect description, remedy) to confirm this specific VIN falls within the recall population.

Tire manufacturer identification: Identify the tire brand, model, DOT code, and manufacture date from the failed tire to determine whether a separate products liability claim against the tire manufacturer is viable.
Other-party insurance information: Confirm the adverse party's carrier and policy limits to assess collectability against the 40% fault share.
Repair/total-loss documentation: Obtain final repair invoices or total-loss valuation to substantiate the $4,700 paid amount and $5,200 gross subrogation figure.

liabilityAssessor.output.rationale: The 2019 Nissan Altima experienced a front-tire tread separation on 2024-12-15, a failure mode directly addressed by NHTSA recall campaign 21V169000, which covers a known TIRES component defect on this exact make, model, and model year. The police report authored by Officer #8927 documents the tread separation at the scene, providing an independent contemporaneous record linking the defect to the loss event. Because the recalled defect is the proximate cause of the blowout, product liability exposure attaches to the tire/vehicle manufacturer, making them the appropriate subrogation target. California's pure comparative negligence doctrine reduces the recoverable share to 40% of the $5,200 gross exposure — yielding the rules-engine demand of $2,080 — because the insured has been assessed at 60% fault. With 406 days remaining on the statute of limitations, there is adequate time to develop the physical evidence and pursue the demand before the deadline.
risks: Causation challenge: The opposing party will argue that the tread separation was caused by road hazard, improper inflation, overloading, or driver neglect rather than the recalled manufacturing defect — especially since evidence strength is only MODERATE and physical tire evidence has not yet been secured.

Recall remedy defense: If the manufacturer can show that the recall remedy (e.g., tire replacement) was made available and the insured failed to respond to the recall notice, they may argue the insured's inaction was a superseding cause, potentially increasing the insured's comparative fault beyond 60%.

Insured's high fault share: At 60% comparative fault, the insured's own conduct (speed, road conditions, vehicle maintenance) will be scrutinized; the defense may seek to push that percentage higher, further eroding the recoverable demand below the $2,080 figure.

Chain-of-custody / evidence preservation: Without the physical tire in custody, the defense will challenge whether the tread separation pattern is consistent with the specific defect described in campaign 21V169000, potentially defeating the recall-to-loss-cause linkage.

Statute of limitations / tolling disputes: Although 406 days remain, delays in obtaining the physical tire, recall remedy records, and expert analysis could compress the timeline; the defense may also contest the accrual date of the claim.

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019-2020 Altima and 2018-2021 Titan vehicles equipped with Continental tires.  On the affected vehicles, it is possible that one or more tires were cured for too long during tire production.
results.Consequence: Over cured tires may develop a break in the sidewall, resulting in sudden air loss or belt edge separation which could lead to tread/belt loss.  Either condition can cause a loss of vehicle control, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners, and dealers will inspect the tires, and replace them as necessary, free of charge.  Owner notification letters were mailed on May 11, 2021.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.  Nissan's number for this recall is PC798.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019 Altima vehicles equipped with front wheel drive (FWD) and 2.5 liter engines.  The fuel pump lock ring may not be fully engaged, possibly causing fuel to leak.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 301, "Fuel System Integrity."
results.Consequence: A fuel leak in the presence of an ignition source increases the risk of a fire.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners, and dealers will inspect the fuel tank assembly. If the lock ring is disengaged, dealers will tighten the ring to specification. If the lock ring is detached, dealers will replace the fuel pump.  Both remedies will be completed free of charge. The recall began May 15, 2019. Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019 Altima vehicles.  The retainer clip connecting the low pressure fuel tube to the high pressure fuel pump may not have been locked into position.
results.Consequence: If the retainer clip is unlocked, the fuel tube may shift and cause a fuel leak, increasing the risk of a fire.  If the fuel tube fully disconnects, the engine can stall, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan has notified owners, and dealers will route the fuel hose into the holding clip and lock the retainer clip into place, as necessary, free of charge.  The recall began February 11, 2019.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019 Nissan Altima vehicles.  The brake switch bracket may be in the incorrect location, which may cause the brake switch to remain on.
results.Consequence: If the brake switch remains in the ON position, the brake lights will remain illuminated when the brakes are not being pressed, which may confuse other drivers.  Additionally, the transmission shift lever may be moved out of the Park position without the brake pedal being pressed, allowing the vehicle to roll unexpectedly.  Either condition increases the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners, and dealers will inspect and install a new brake pedal as needed, free of charge.  The recall began May 15, 2019.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Component: BACK OVER PREVENTION: SENSING SYSTEM: CAMERA
results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2018-2019 Nissan Altima, Armada, Frontier, Kicks, Leaf, Maxima, Murano, NV, NV200, Pathfinder, Rogue, Rogue Sport, Sentra, Titan, Titan Diesel, Versa Note and Versa Sedan vehicles, as well as Infiniti Q50, Q60, QX30 and QX80 vehicles.  Additionally included are 2019 Nissan GT-R and Taxi and Infiniti QX50, QX60, Q70, Q70L vehicles.  The back-up camera and display settings can be adjusted such that the rear view image is no longer visible and the system will retain that setting the next time the vehicle is placed in reverse.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 111, "Rear Visibility."
results.Consequence: The lack of an image in the back-up camera display increases the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners in phases, having dealers update the back-up camera settings software, free of charge.  The recall began November 11, 2019 and all affected VINs should be activated.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669 or INFINITI customer service at 1-800-662-6200.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Component: BACK OVER PREVENTION: SENSING SYSTEM: CAMERA
results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019-2021 Altima and 2020-2021 Sentra vehicles.  Damage to the camera harness can cause distortion or loss of the rearview camera display image.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard number 111, "Rear Visibility."
results.Consequence: A rearview camera that does not properly display an image can reduce the driver's rear view, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Dealers will inspect the rearview camera and harness for damage and replace them as necessary.  If no damage is found, the dealer will apply protective tape and reroute the rearview camera harness.  Repairs will be performed free of charge.  Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed October 19, 2023.  Owners may contact Nissan's customer service at 1-800-867-7669.  Nissan's number for this recall is R23C3.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.nhtsa.gov.

results.Component: ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING:ENGINE:HARD PARTS INTERNAL/MECHANICAL
results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2021-2024 Rogue, 2019-2020 Altima, 2019-2022 Infiniti QX50, and 2022 Infiniti QX55 vehicles equipped with 3-cylinder 1.5L or 4-cylinder 2.0L variable compression turbo (VC-Turbo) engines. The engine bearings may have manufacturing defects that can lead to engine failure.
results.Consequence: Engine failure increases the risk of a crash. A bearing failure may cause a breach in the engine block, allowing hot oil to be discharged, increasing the risk of an engine fire.
results.Remedy: Dealers will reprogram the engine control module (ECM) software, free of charge. Owner letters were mailed April 8, 2026. Owners may contact Nissan's customer service at 800-647-7261 or Infiniti's customer service at 1-800-662-6200. Nissan's numbers for this recall are R25A8/A9 and R25B1/B2.

Tire manufacturer identification: Identify the tire brand, model, DOT code, and manufacture date from the failed tire to determine whether a separate products liability claim against the tire manufacturer is viable.

liability.rationale: The 2019 Nissan Altima experienced a front-tire tread separation on 2024-12-15, a failure mode directly addressed by NHTSA recall campaign 21V169000, which covers a known TIRES component defect on this exact make, model, and model year. The police report authored by Officer #8927 documents the tread separation at the scene, providing an independent contemporaneous record linking the defect to the loss event. Because the recalled defect is the proximate cause of the blowout, product liability exposure attaches to the tire/vehicle manufacturer, making them the appropriate subrogation target. risks: Causation challenge: The opposing party will argue that the tread separation was caused by road hazard, improper inflation, overloading, or driver neglect rather than the recalled manufacturing defect, especially since evidence strength is only MODERATE and physical tire evidence has not yet been secured.

Recall remedy defense: If the manufacturer can show that the recall remedy (e.g., tire replacement) was made available and the insured failed to respond to the recall notice, they may argue the insured's inaction was a superseding cause, potentially increasing the insured's comparative fault beyond 60%.

Insured's high fault share: At 60% comparative fault, the insured's own conduct (speed, road conditions, vehicle maintenance) will be scrutinized; the defense may seek to push that percentage higher, further eroding the recoverable demand below the $2,080 figure.

Chain-of-custody / evidence preservation: Without the physical tire in custody, the defense will challenge whether the tread separation pattern is consistent with the specific defect described in campaign 21V169000, potentially defeating the recall-to-loss-cause linkage.

Statute of limitations / tolling disputes: Although 406 days remain, delays in obtaining the physical tire, recall remedy records, and expert analysis could compress the timeline; the defense may also contest the accrual date of the claim.

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019-2020 Altima and 2018-2021 Titan vehicles equipped with Continental tires.  On the affected vehicles, it is possible that one or more tires were cured for too long during tire production.
results.Consequence: Over cured tires may develop a break in the sidewall, resulting in sudden air loss or belt edge separation which could lead to tread/belt loss.  Either condition can cause a loss of vehicle control, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners, and dealers will inspect the tires, and replace them as necessary, free of charge.  Owner notification letters were mailed on May 11, 2021.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.  Nissan's number for this recall is PC798.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019 Altima vehicles equipped with front wheel drive (FWD) and 2.5 liter engines.  The fuel pump lock ring may not be fully engaged, possibly causing fuel to leak.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 301, "Fuel System Integrity."
results.Consequence: A fuel leak in the presence of an ignition source increases the risk of a fire.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners, and dealers will inspect the fuel tank assembly. If the lock ring is disengaged, dealers will tighten the ring to specification. If the lock ring is detached, dealers will replace the fuel pump.  Both remedies will be completed free of charge. The recall began May 15, 2019. Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019 Altima vehicles.  The retainer clip connecting the low pressure fuel tube to the high pressure fuel pump may not have been locked into position.
results.Consequence: If the retainer clip is unlocked, the fuel tube may shift and cause a fuel leak, increasing the risk of a fire.  If the fuel tube fully disconnects, the engine can stall, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan has notified owners, and dealers will route the fuel hose into the holding clip and lock the retainer clip into place, as necessary, free of charge.  The recall began February 11, 2019.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov

results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019 Nissan Altima vehicles.  The brake switch bracket may be in the incorrect location, which may cause the brake switch to remain on.
results.Consequence: If the brake switch remains in the ON position, the brake lights will remain illuminated when the brakes are not being pressed, which may confuse other drivers.  Additionally, the transmission shift lever may be moved out of the Park position without the brake pedal being pressed, allowing the vehicle to roll unexpectedly.  Either condition increases the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners, and dealers will inspect and install a new brake pedal as needed, free of charge.  The recall began May 15, 2019.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Component: BACK OVER PREVENTION: SENSING SYSTEM: CAMERA
results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2018-2019 Nissan Altima, Armada, Frontier, Kicks, Leaf, Maxima, Murano, NV, NV200, Pathfinder, Rogue, Rogue Sport, Sentra, Titan, Titan Diesel, Versa Note and Versa Sedan vehicles, as well as Infiniti Q50, Q60, QX30 and QX80 vehicles.  Additionally included are 2019 Nissan GT-R and Taxi and Infiniti QX50, QX60, Q70, Q70L vehicles.  The back-up camera and display settings can be adjusted such that the rear view image is no longer visible and the system will retain that setting the next time the vehicle is placed in reverse.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 111, "Rear Visibility."
results.Consequence: The lack of an image in the back-up camera display increases the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Nissan will notify owners in phases, having dealers update the back-up camera settings software, free of charge.  The recall began November 11, 2019 and all affected VINs should be activated.  Owners may contact Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669 or INFINITI customer service at 1-800-662-6200.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Component: BACK OVER PREVENTION: SENSING SYSTEM: CAMERA
results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2019-2021 Altima and 2020-2021 Sentra vehicles.  Damage to the camera harness can cause distortion or loss of the rearview camera display image.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard number 111, "Rear Visibility."
results.Consequence: A rearview camera that does not properly display an image can reduce the driver's rear view, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Dealers will inspect the rearview camera and harness for damage and replace them as necessary.  If no damage is found, the dealer will apply protective tape and reroute the rearview camera harness.  Repairs will be performed free of charge.  Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed October 19, 2023.  Owners may contact Nissan's customer service at 1-800-867-7669.  Nissan's number for this recall is R23C3.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.nhtsa.gov.

results.Component: ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING:ENGINE:HARD PARTS INTERNAL/MECHANICAL
results.Summary: Nissan North America, Inc. (Nissan) is recalling certain 2021-2024 Rogue, 2019-2020 Altima, 2019-2022 Infiniti QX50, and 2022 Infiniti QX55 vehicles equipped with 3-cylinder 1.5L or 4-cylinder 2.0L variable compression turbo (VC-Turbo) engines. The engine bearings may have manufacturing defects that can lead to engine failure.
results.Consequence: Engine failure increases the risk of a crash. A bearing failure may cause a breach in the engine block, allowing hot oil to be discharged, increasing the risk of an engine fire.
results.Remedy: Dealers will reprogram the engine control module (ECM) software, free of charge. Owner letters were mailed April 8, 2026. Owners may contact Nissan's customer service at 800-647-7261 or Infiniti's customer service at 1-800-662-6200. Nissan's numbers for this recall are R25A8/A9 and R25B1/B2.

The tread separation failure mode described at the scene is consistent with the type of tire structural defect addressed by campaign 21V169000. Under California's pure comparative negligence doctrine, the insured is assessed at 60% fault, leaving a 40% recoverable fault factor attributable to the other party, yielding a calculated demand of $2,080 against a gross subrogation exposure of $5,200. evidence.evidence_summary: The 2019 Nissan Altima (VIN: 1N4BL4BV5KB570668) sustained a loss on 2024-12-15 attributed to a tire blowout, specifically tread separation observed on the front tire as documented in the synthetic police report by Officer #8927. NHTSA recall campaign 21V169000 covers a TIRES component defect on vehicles matching this make, model, and model year, directly linking the recalled tire defect to the mechanism of loss. The tread separation failure mode described at the scene is consistent with the type of tire structural defect addressed by campaign 21V169000. Under California's pure comparative negligence doctrine, the insured is assessed at 60% fault, leaving a 40% recoverable fault factor attributable to the other party, yielding a calculated demand of $2,080 against a gross subrogation exposure of $5,200. The statute of limitations has approximately 406 days remaining, providing adequate time to pursue recovery. Overall, the recall-to-loss-cause linkage is supported by the police report and the matched NHTSA campaign, but physical tire evidence and recall remedy records are needed to solidify the claim.
gaps: Physical tire evidence: The failed front tire should be preserved, inspected, and photographed by a qualified tire forensic expert to confirm tread separation consistent with the defect described in NHTSA campaign 21V169000.

Recall remedy records: Obtain documentation from Nissan or the dealership network confirming whether the recall remedy was or was not performed on VIN 1N4BL4BV5KB570668 prior to the loss date, an unperformed remedy strengthens the subrogation theory against the manufacturer or dealer.
NHTSA campaign 21V169000 full details: Retrieve the complete campaign document (affected VIN range, defect description, remedy) to confirm this specific VIN falls within the recall population.

Tire manufacturer identification: Identify the tire brand, model, DOT code, and manufacture date from the failed tire to determine whether a separate products liability claim against the tire manufacturer is viable.
Other-party insurance information: Confirm the adverse party's carrier and policy limits to assess collectability against the 40% fault share.
Repair/total-loss documentation: Obtain final repair invoices or total-loss valuation to substantiate the $4,700 paid amount and $5,200 gross subrogation figure.

liability.liable_party: Tire manufacturer / vehicle manufacturer (Nissan and/or the tire supplier covered under NHTSA recall campaign 21V169000)
liability.rationale: The 2019 Nissan Altima experienced a front-tire tread separation on 2024-12-15, a failure mode directly addressed by NHTSA recall campaign 21V169000, which covers a known TIRES component defect on this exact make, model, and model year. The police report authored by Officer #8927 documents the tread separation at the scene, providing an independent contemporaneous record linking the defect to the loss event. Because the recalled defect is the proximate cause of the blowout, product liability exposure attaches to the tire/vehicle manufacturer, making them the appropriate subrogation target. California's pure comparative negligence doctrine reduces the recoverable share to 40% of the $5,200 gross exposure, yielding the rules-engine demand of $2,080, because the insured has been assessed at 60% fault. With 406 days remaining on the statute of limitations, there is adequate time to develop the physical evidence and pursue the demand before the deadline.
risks: Causation challenge: The opposing party will argue that the tread separation was caused by road hazard, improper inflation, overloading, or driver neglect rather than the recalled manufacturing defect, especially since evidence strength is only MODERATE and physical tire evidence has not yet been secured.

Recall remedy defense: If the manufacturer can show that the recall remedy (e.g., tire replacement) was made available and the insured failed to respond to the recall notice, they may argue the insured's inaction was a superseding cause, potentially increasing the insured's comparative fault beyond 60%.

Insured's high fault share: At 60% comparative fault, the insured's own conduct (speed, road conditions, vehicle maintenance) will be scrutinized; the defense may seek to push that percentage higher, further eroding the recoverable demand below the $2,080 figure.

Chain-of-custody / evidence preservation: Without the physical tire in custody, the defense will challenge whether the tread separation pattern is consistent with the specific defect described in campaign 21V169000, potentially defeating the recall-to-loss-cause linkage.

Statute of limitations / tolling disputes: Although 406 days remain, delays in obtaining the physical tire, recall remedy records, and expert analysis could compress the timeline; the defense may also contest the accrual date of the claim.
